name: Western yellowstriped armyworm
description_damage: See: Common Pests of Vegetable Crops
monitoring: Monitoring to catch infestations early is important, because Bacillus thuringiensis ( Bt ) insecticides work much more effectively on small larvae.

management.biological: Common natural enemies of armyworms include several braconid and ichneumonid wasps and many general predators, including assassin bugs, damsel bugs, spiders, and a nucleopolyhedrovirus, reported to have brought about excellent late year control in Canada. None of these natural enemies can be counted upon to achieve adequate control in any given year.

management.cultural: Weed control is important. Lambsquarters and wild mustard attract egg-laying females and provide a source of food for larvae. As weeds dry, large populations of armyworms can move onto crops. When infested alfalfa fields are mowed, large dispersions of armyworms also can take place. Fall tillage can help destroy overwintering pupae.
